lesson: PROD PRs in eda-dbt-em are *bundles* of validated qa PRs, not raw feature work. Title convention: 'PROD promotion: <ticket(s)> [#qa1, #qa2, ...]' — always cite source qa PR numbers in brackets. Example: PR #424 = 'PROD promotion: EDAEM-3620 + EDAEM-3622 + EDAEM-3627 + ACV restatement Q1-FY27 fix [#417, #418, #419, #420, #422, #425]'. Reviewers can then diff each qa PR independently.

PROD promotion is typically a cherry-pick onto prod base with an *identical line-count diff* vs the qa PR. If line counts diverge, something drifted — investigate. Examples: #441 / #444 both note 'Identical 1-line × 4-file diff to QA PR #N'. Use git diff <qa-pr-merge-sha> origin/prod to verify before opening the prod PR.

Observed PROD promotion cadence April-May 2026: 27 prod PRs in 4 months (≈6/month). Promotion delay is typically 1-3 days after qa merge for stable changes; same-day for hot fixes (e.g., NRR/GRR rollback #443→#444 same calendar day). qa carries 5-6× the PR volume of prod — qa is the heavily-iterated branch.
evidence: eda-dbt-em PR history (qa+prod) 2026-02-10 → 2026-06-23; fetched via gh CLI 2026-06-25; 131 PRs analysed.

lesson: Re-enabling a cross-project dependency requires CX-side prod deploy FIRST, then EM dependencies.yml flip (PR #460 + #461 - 'Reenable CX dependency as CX has deployed the changes into PROD'). Check eda-dbt-cx prod state via gh api before unblocking dependencies.yml additions in EM.
